intro.title: Discriminated Union Props
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple Vue component that displays different types of user notifications, such as success messages, warnings, and errors. You'll learn how to use discriminated union props, a TypeScript pattern that ensures your component only receives valid combinations of data based on a shared property (like 'type'). The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API with TypeScript, using defineProps for type-safe props. By the end, you'll understand how to define and use a union of object types to make your components more robust and self-documenting.
intro.usecase: Discriminated union props are essential when building UI components that need to handle multiple distinct states or variants with clear type safety. You'll see this pattern in dashboard cards that display different content types (metrics, charts, alerts), form steps with varying input requirements, or notification systems showing success/error/warning messages. This approach ensures your components handle each variant correctly while providing excellent TypeScript support and preventing runtime errors.
